home_pitcher_note: Guthrie outlasted all the competition to line up for Baltimore's Opening Day start, an assignment granted to him as a reward for a fine rookie season, during which he ranked second among AL rookies in ERA, strikeouts and innings.
away_pitcher_note: Shields will be making his first Opening Day start and it will happen in Camden Yards, where he made his Major League debut in 2006. He's is 1-1 with a 3.67 ERA in seven career starts against the O's.
summary: 2008-03-31 - Tampa Bay Rays (6) @ Baltimore Orioles (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Cabrera stayed healthy enough to take every rotation turn last season, a fact which helped him throw 200 innings for the first time. The righty remained wild, though, and led the league in walks for the second straight season.
away_pitcher_note: Garza will be making his first start with the Rays after coming to the team with shortstop Jason Bartlett in the deal that sent Delmon Young, Brendan Harris and Jason Pridie to the Twins.
summary: 2008-04-02 - Tampa Bay Rays (6) @ Baltimore Orioles (9) (Final)
2008-04-03 - Tampa Bay Rays @ Baltimore Orioles (Postponed)

home_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old Kennedy makes just his fourth big league start as the Yankees play the second game of a four-game series with the Rays. A late callup last season, Kennedy made his big league debut on Sept. 1 against Tampa Bay and recorded the win in a 9-6 New York victory, pitching seven innings of three-run, five-hit ball. He recorded 13 of his final 14 batters faced, allowing just a solo home run to B.J. Upton in the sixth inning.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander got off to a rocky start in 2007 after getting the call from Triple-A Durham. He picked up the win in his first Major League decision June 10 at Florida then he lost his next eight decisions. However, Sonnanstine learned quickly and adjusted accordingly by going more with his fastball to set up the vast array of pitches he throws from all different angles. He is 1-1 with a 3.14 ERA against the Yankees in 2007.
summary: 2008-04-04 - Tampa Bay Rays (13) @ New York Yankees (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Having been pushed back from the No. 2 spot by back spasms, Pettitte is expected to open his campaign against the Rays. The lefty is looking to reprise the role of stopper that helped the Yankees record 21 wins in his 34 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson got off to a terrible start in 2007, when he went 1-9 with a 7.23 ERA in 17 games (16 starts) in the first half of the season. His results were much improved in the second half, when he went 4-6 with a 4.48 ERA in 15 starts, including a four-hit shutout of the Rangers on Aug. 11. Yet he continues to be an enigma, the pitcher with the big fastball who gets mixed results. Jackson has pitched well at Yankee Stadium, posting a 1-1 mark with a 4.38 ERA in four appearances (two starts).
summary: 2008-04-05 - Tampa Bay Rays (6) @ New York Yankees (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Wang's regular season debut was his best start of the year so far, according to manager Joe Girardi, who wasn't putting much stock into Wang's shaky Grapefruit League campaign. The right-hander limited the Blue Jays to two runs over seven innings as he secured the victory in the final Opening Day at Yankee Stadium on April 1. Wang made three starts against the Rays in 2007, faring 2-1 with a 4.42 ERA. His best start was his final one of the campaign, twirling six innings of two-run, seven-hit ball at Tropicana Field on Sept. 26. The sinkerballing Wang is 27-9 at Yankee Stadium since the beginning of the 2005 campaign.
away_pitcher_note: After a rough beginning in which Shields surrendered two runs in the first inning on Opening Day against the Orioles, Shields settled in to add six scoreless frames to earn the win. Shields' best pitch has always been his changeup, but he also has a plus fastball and curve and he's added a cutter that has helped him throw inside to left-handers. Shields is 0-4 with an 8.58 ERA in five career starts against the Yankees; he is 0-2 with a 10.57 ERA in three starts at Yankee Stadium.
summary: 2008-04-06 - Tampa Bay Rays (0) @ New York Yankees (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Mussina will make his second start of the new campaign on Monday as the Yankees complete the four-game wraparound series with the Rays. The 39-year-old took a loss in his first outing, hurling 5 2/3 innings against the Blue Jays at Yankee Stadium, but giving up three earned runs, including a two-run homer to Vernon Wells in the third inning. Mussina will try again to match Bob Gibson's career mark of 251 victories as he faces Tampa Bay, a club he was 0-1 with a 7.59 ERA against in two starts last year.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel struggled for much of the 2007 season trying to incorporate mechanical changes into his motion. Once he finally blended in those changes, the results were much improved. He went five or more innings in his final seven starts, and went 2-0 over that same period, including a win on the final day of the season at Toronto. He is 1-1 with a 6.41 ERA in six appearances at Yankee Stadium (four starts). But he was 1-0 with a 3.00 ERA in two starts at Yankee Stadium in 2007.
summary: 2008-04-07 - Tampa Bay Rays (1) @ New York Yankees (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Garza will be making his second start for the Rays in the home opener after making his debut Wednesday night against the Orioles. He got a no-decision after allowing five earned runs on six hits, including two home runs, in 5 1/3 innings. The 24-year-old right-hander has a fastball that occasionally touches 97 mph, a curveball, a slider and a changeup. He is 1-1 with a 9.64 ERA in two career starts against the Mariners.
away_pitcher_note: Bedard was originally slated to start Sunday against his former team, the Orioles, but was pushed back.  Bedard bobbed and weaved his way through five innings on Opening Day, settling for a no-decision. He threw 106 pitches, but the only run he allowed was a solo home run.
summary: 2008-04-08 - Seattle Mariners (6) @ Tampa Bay Rays (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Sonnanstine is a master of deception employing an array of pitches that he can throw from all different angles. But he has learned to primarily use his fastball to setup the other pitches. Since making that adjustment he has been a lot more successful. Friday night he survived a four-run third against the Yankees and did not allow any further damage in six innings to pick up his first win of the season. Sonnanstine has one career start against the Mariners, which came Sept. 16 at Seattle when he held the Mariners to one run on six hits in seven innings to pick up the win in a 9-2 Rays victory.
away_pitcher_note: The first Mariners starter this season to surrender more than one run in a game, Washburn tries to notch his first win of the season against the Rays in the middle game of a three-game series. Washburn surrendered three runs against the Orioles after his three predecessors -- Erik Bedard, Felix Hernandez and Carlos Silva -- each held the Rangers to one run. Washburn had been 1-0 with a 1.89 ERA in his previous three first regular season starts.
summary: 2008-04-09 - Seattle Mariners (7) @ Tampa Bay Rays (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Jackson got off to a shaky start Saturday against the Yankees when he surrendered a run in the first and then loaded the bases with one out in the second. But the right-hander escaped the second-inning jam without allowing any runs and didn't allow any more runs during his six-inning stint -- retiring the final nine hitters he faced -- to pick up his first win of the season. Jackson will be making his first start against the Mariners in this one.
away_pitcher_note: Three of the four walks the veteran right-hander surrendered in his first start of the season came in the same inning and helped erase the second of the two-run leads he had to work with against the Orioles. It didn't help that the usually reliable Seattle defense committed two errors on the same play, leading to an unearned run. Batista threw hard but didn't change speeds well enough to keep opposing hitters off balance.
summary: 2008-04-10 - Seattle Mariners (0) @ Tampa Bay Rays (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Shields had quality stuff Sunday against the Yankees, allowing two runs on eight hits with one walk and five strikeouts, but he took the loss thanks to the two-run homer he surrendered to Hideki Matsui. Shields' best pitch has always been his changeup, but he also has a plus fastball and curve and he's added a cutter that has helped him throw inside to left-handers. Shields is 2-1 with a 3.54 ERA in eight career starts against the Orioles. He is 11-6 with a 3.68 ERA in 26 starts at Tropicana Field.
away_pitcher_note: Guthrie struggled in his season debut and improved in his second outing, but he had the misfortune of being up against Seattle's Felix Hernandez. Hernandez threw eight scoreless innings, and Guthrie settled for a seven inning no-decision. The right-hander was the first of Baltimore's starters to complete six innings.
summary: 2008-04-11 - Baltimore Orioles (5) @ Tampa Bay Rays (10) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Hammel got off to a rough start against the Yankees Monday night when he surrendered a two-run homer to Bobby Abreu in the first. But he settled into a rhythm, showing good composure and command of his pitches while adding four scoreless frames to his line. The Yankees added two more in the sixth to hand Hammel his first loss of the season, but overall he had an encouraging outing. Hammel is 0-3 with an 8.84 ERA in four starts against the Orioles; he is 0-5 with a 6.87 ERA at Tropicana Field.
away_pitcher_note: Cabrera completed six innings in his last start, but he also gave up two home runs and four earned runs. The right-hander has given up 10 earned runs in his first two outings of the year, and he's walked nine batters against seven strikeouts. Cabrera has led the American League in walks for two straight seasons and is a distinct threat this year.
summary: 2008-04-12 - Baltimore Orioles (3) @ Tampa Bay Rays (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: With scheduled starter Matt Garza on the 15-day disabled list with a radial nerve irritation in his right arm, the Rays are yet to name an official starter. In the past, the club has brought up the pitcher who is in the same slot in Triple-A Durham, to create minimal rotation disruption. For this start, that would mean Niemann, the lanky right-hander who was vying for a rotation spot this spring. If Niemann does start for Tampa Bay vs. the Orioles, it will be the 25-year-old's Major League debut. Niemann is 1-1 in Durham with a 3.27 ERA, and tossed six innings in the Bulls' Tuesday night victory over Columbus, 5-4.
away_pitcher_note: Burres pitched well in his first start of the season, allowing one run in six-plus innings of work. The southpaw gave up seven hits but came up with key outs when he needed them, most notably two double plays and a key bases-loaded strikeout. Burres celebrated his 27th birthday by recording his first win of the year.
summary: 2008-04-13 - Baltimore Orioles (2) @ Tampa Bay Rays (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Coming off his first loss of the season, to Seattle on Wednesday, Sonnanstine will face the Yankees for the second time this season. The right-hander had a solid debut in New York on April 4, going six solid innings and scattering six hits and four runs. Sonnanstine gave up all four runs in the third inning, but settled down to retire the last 10 Yankees batters in order.
away_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old Kennedy had a curveball thrown his way in his last appearance on April 9, informed about 20 minutes before first pitch that he wasn't starting due to weather concerns. The rains came but play never halted, leaving manager Joe Girardi to use Kennedy for the final three innings of a 4-0 loss at Kansas City. Kennedy has allowed eight earned runs in his first 5 1/3 innings of 2008 after allowing just 31 in 146 2/3 professional frames last season, including pitching 19 innings at the Major League level and recording a 1.89 ERA with New York. The Rays battered Kennedy for six runs on four hits in an abbreviated 2 1/3-inning start on April 4 at Yankee Stadium.
summary: 2008-04-14 - New York Yankees (8) @ Tampa Bay Rays (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Jackson is coming off a stellar two-hit performance vs. Seattle on April 10, in which the right-hander went eight strong innings, allowing two hits and striking out six. The last time he faced New York on April 5, Jackson beat Andy Pettitte 6-3 at Yankee Stadium, and retired the last nine batters he faced. Jackson allowed just one run off four hits in that game, striking out four.

summary: 2009-08-05 - Boston Red Sox (4) @ Tampa Bay Rays (6) (Final)

Felix started one game against Tampa Bay last season, held the eventual AL champs to one run over eight innings, but had to settle for a no-decision. away_pitcher_note: The unforeseen sterling season for Jeff Niemann continued Saturday, as the rookie right-hander became the first Rays pitcher to reach double digits in wins this season. He ended up giving up two hits and two runs -- one earned -- but took the loss as the Rays simply couldn't muster any support. The leadoff hitter reached base in three of the four innings he pitched and two of them scored. Rowland-Smith was 0-0 with one save in three appearances against the Rays last season and has faced them four times in his MLB career.

summary: 2009-08-09 - Tampa Bay Rays (2) @ Seattle Mariners (11) (Final)

summary: 2009-08-12 - Tampa Bay Rays (5) @ Los Angeles Angels (10) (Final)

Against Baltimore, Halladay logged nine innings and allowed three runs (two earned) on nine hits with four strikeouts and one walk. summary: 2009-08-16 - Toronto Blue Jays (2) @ Tampa Bay Rays (5) (Final)

summary: 2009-08-18 - Baltimore Orioles (4) @ Tampa Bay Rays (5) (Final)
